title: Minimum Time to Revert Word to Initial State I
summary: Given a 0-indexed string word and an integer k, at each second, you must remove the first k characters from word and then add any k characters to the end of word.
statement: Given a 0-indexed string word and an integer k, at each second, you must remove the first k characters from word and then add any k characters to the end of word. Determine the minimum time greater than zero required for word to revert to its initial state.
constraints: word is a nonempty lowercase string and 1≤k≤length.
Each second removes the first k current characters and appends any k chosen characters.
Return the minimum positive seconds after which the original word can be restored.
hints: After t removals, only the original suffix beginning at t*k is forced to remain; appended characters can fill everything else.
Check whether that forced suffix equals the original prefix of the same length at each multiple of k.
For removed=k,2k,...<n, return removed/k on word[removed:]==word[:-removed]; otherwise return ceil(n/k).
The equality is necessary for untouched characters and sufficient because all removed positions may be replaced arbitrarily; once all originals are removed restoration is always possible.
editorial: The equality is necessary for untouched characters and sufficient because all removed positions may be replaced arbitrarily; once all originals are removed restoration is always possible.

tests.explanation: After two removals, suffix a matches the original prefix a; the remaining six characters can be appended to restore the word.
After one removal, suffix aba equals the original prefix aba, so the appended four characters can finish restoration immediately.
